transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Jonas Park (Redwood SE); Rae Thompson (Redwood CSM); Elliot Rivera (Arcturus Head of ML); Priya Shah (Platform Engineer); Noah Kim (SRE); Sam Ortega (PM)
Shared links: https://redwood.internal/poc/arcturus/telemetry (RBW: telemetry export), https://drive.company/arcturus/prompt-samples (sample set)

Summary (auto): weekly POC sync—review of prefix/KV hit-rate changes after last tune, brief troubleshooting of evictions causing cache churn, decision to run 24h soak with TTL tweak, action items assigned.

Topics: prefix reuse metrics; KV hit-rate regression on long-tail; eviction/TTL strategy; prompt normalization; Dedicated vs Hosted perf benchmark planning; security/compliance reminder (SOC2 ask)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Patel: okay hey everyone, thanks for making time. can we do quick round of intros for the recording?
[00:06] Elliot Rivera: yep elliot here, lead on model infra at arcturus.
[00:09] Priya Shah: priya, platform eng.
[00:11] Noah Kim: noah, s r e, i'll be running the staging soak.
[00:13] Sam Ortega: sam, product.
[00:15] Maya Patel: cool, and from redwood we got jonas and rae. jonas you wanna kick off with the numbers?
[00:20] Jonas Park: yeah sure. quick TLDR — overall KV hit-rate for week ended up 38% which is +12 points from baseline we saw two weeks ago, so prefetched prefixes and normalization are helping. p95 latency is 212ms which is roughly 8ms up from last week so small tradeoff.
[00:35] Priya Shah: 38% sounds good but i was looking at the per-cohort breakdown and the long tail cohort is still only 9%. that's the part generating lots of misses and hence extra tokens.
[00:45] Jonas Park: yeah that's correct. the cohort that has heavy personalization — long user histories — has lower prefix reuse. we suspect prompt drift and injected user-specific tokens are fragmenting keys.
[00:58] Elliot Rivera: can you clarify what "prefix" means in the telemetry? sometimes the names are slightly different — prefix vs session snapshot — and our analytics team is mapping the wrong field.
[01:08] Jonas Park: right, in our export 'prefix' is the canonicalized initial token sequence we store as a KV key. sometimes Fireflies or our exporter labels it session_snapshot, sorry for confusion. the canonicalization strips stopwords and normalizes dates where possible.
[01:23] Noah Kim: quick question — are you storing user IDs inside the prefix accidentally? we saw some keys with numerical suffixes.
[01:30] Jonas Park: good catch. there was an earlier version of the preprocessor that appended session ids for debug; we believe we turned that off last patch but i'll double-check the pipeline.
[01:38] Maya Patel: okay so root causes: prompt fragmentation, occasional debug suffixes, and TTL behavior causing eviction churn. jonas, do you have the eviction timeline from the last 72 hours?
[01:49] Jonas Park: yes — attaching numbers: eviction spikes align with our peak traffic windows at 10am PST and 6pm UTC. we saw a sharp drop in hit-rate immediately after each spike, so it's likely we're thrashing on small working set.
[02:04] Priya Shah: right and the p95 during those spikes goes up to 320ms which triggers SLO alerts on our side. we need to avoid the spikes.
[02:12] Rae Thompson: just flagged the alert logs you sent — looks like a cascade: higher miss rate -> more tokens -> more GPU time -> backpressure to the ingress.
[02:22] Sam Ortega: cost question — the CFO wants to understand: when hit-rate drops from 40% to 15% what's the incremental cost delta? do we have an apples-to-apples?
[02:30] Jonas Park: ballpark, for your current model and traffic shape, each percent drop in hit-rate adds roughly 0.7% token cost because of re-requests. so a drop of 25 points can be 17-18% uplift in token spend, plus tail latency penalties.
[02:44] Sam Ortega: ok that helps. thanks.
[02:46] Elliot Rivera: on prompt normalization — we've been experimenting with trimming salutation lines and user signatures. any guidance on how aggressive we should be? we worry about losing context.
[02:56] Jonas Park: yeah, there's a balance. we recommend a two-tier approach: 1) light normalization (strip salutations, normalize common date formats) which preserves semantics and increases reuse; 2) heavier normalization can be applied to cohorted traffic where semantics are less sensitive. we can provide a rule set.
[03:14] Priya Shah: can you share that rule set and a quick script we can run in our preprocessor?
[03:19] Maya Patel: yes, we'll upload diff script to the shared drive after the call.
[03:23] Jonas Park: also, i want to surface one surprising metric — after we enabled prefix coalescing the average length of stored KV keys dropped ~14 tokens which improved TTL efficiency. however, a subset of keys are still very long because of appended JSON blobs.
[03:38] Noah Kim: appended JSON blobs — we actually found some microservices returning full metadata in assistant messages. that's on us, but we can gate that.
[03:46] Elliot Rivera: any immediate mitigations? we need something low-risk to stabilize hit-rate before the CFO meeting next tuesday.
[03:53] Jonas Park: mitigation plan we tested: reduce eviction aggressiveness (increase TTL from 30s to 45s), enable session affinity for known heavy cohorts, and apply a prompt rewrite step to trim obvious noise. in quick staging runs the overall hit-rate moved from 26% to 41% within 6 hours.
[04:12] Priya Shah: staging runs — did that change memory profile? our infra might not handle longer TTLs if the working set grows too large.
[04:19] Jonas Park: yes memory grew about 12% in the test due to retained keys, but we did not hit OOM. we should plan the soak to validate at production QPS.
[04:28] Maya Patel: okay so action is to run a 24 hour soak with TTL 45 and prompt normalization enabled. noah will run that on staging and we'll compare hit-rate and p95.
[04:38] Noah Kim: yep i'll kick that off after this call.
[04:41] Sam Ortega: question on evaluation — what do you want us to surface after soak? hit-rate by cohort, latency histograms, and a sample of missed prompts?
[04:48] Jonas Park: exactly — cohort-level hit-rate, p50/p95/p99 latencies, memory footprint, and a 500-sample set of missed prompts with raw and canonicalized forms.
[04:58] Priya Shah: also can you provide a mapping of the prefix canonicalization rules? our analytics will need that to join on key.
[05:05] Maya Patel: yes we'll push mapping doc.
[05:08] Elliot Rivera: on security/compliance we had a quick legal ask about retention. do you purge any PII from KV keys?
[05:16] Jonas Park: we do not store PII intentionally; canonicalization strips emails and numeric ids when identified. but we should run a red-team scan to ensure nothing slipped in.
[05:25] Priya Shah: can you also confirm KMS used for logs in the hosted mode? we require keys to be customer-managed for production.
[05:33] Rae Thompson: noted — for Private deployments we support customer KMS; for Hosted we have BYOK options in our roadmap, and we'll share the SOC2/ISO artifacts.
[05:43] Sam Ortega: great. back to the cache logic — we saw cases of near-duplicate prefixes because of minor punctuation differences. is there any fuzzy matching option?
[05:52] Jonas Park: we have a hashing coalescer that normalizes punctuation and lowercases; fuzzy merge is experimental because it risks false positives. we can prototype a threshold-based merge for non-critical cohorts.
[06:04] Elliot Rivera: cool. for the Dedicated vs Hosted benchmark — we need an apples-to-apples setup: same model version, same batching config, identical traffic replay. can redwood coordinate that?
[06:15] Jonas Park: yes, we'll provide a benchmark recipe and a recording of the replay driver. but note Dedicated nodes will have different kernel selection so latency numbers will diverge slightly.
[06:26] Priya Shah: understood. can we also measure cost per 1M tokens across both?
[06:30] Jonas Park: yes we'll include cost delta in the report.
[06:33] Maya Patel: ok moving to risks and blockers — anything blocking next steps?
[06:37] Priya Shah: need the canonicalization script and sample set. also legal requested SOC2 snapshot which we don't have yet.
[06:44] Rae Thompson: i'll assemble the SOC2 packet and BYOK roadmap note and share link.
[06:49] Elliot Rivera: one more note — when you did the quick staging run last week the model output quality shifted slightly for some templates; product noticed hallucination increase of about 0.5% for template group B. did you see that?
[06:59] Jonas Park: yes we observed a small delta correlated to more aggressive prefix coalescing on template group B; hypothesis is coalescing removed disambiguating tokens. we're rolling back coalescing for that cohort while investigating alternative key-preserving transforms.
[07:13] Sam Ortega: that's important — quality > cost for us on certain flows.
[07:16] Maya Patel: noted. we'll make quality gates mandatory for those cohorts. jonas will run a focused A/B with quality metrics.
[07:24] Jonas Park: will do — propose running A/B for 48 hours on 20% of traffic.
[07:29] Priya Shah: fine.
[07:31] Maya Patel: quick recap and next steps: 1) Jonas to double-check the preprocessor for session-id suffix bug and share a fix (by 2026-07-16). 2) Maya to upload canonicalization rules and diff script (by 2026-07-16). 3) Noah to run 24h TTL=45s soak in staging and share hit-rate and latency (by 2026-07-20). 4) Jonas + Noah to prepare Dedicated vs Hosted benchmark plan (by 2026-07-19). 5) Rae to share SOC2 snapshot and BYOK notes (by 2026-07-16).
[07:55] Sam Ortega: and please include cost delta estimates for worst-case miss scenarios.
[07:59] Jonas Park: will include.
[08:01] Maya Patel: any other questions?
[08:03] Elliot Rivera: nope, thanks all.
[08:05] Priya Shah: thanks.
[08:07] Noah Kim: thanks.
[08:09] Maya Patel: great we'll follow up in thread. bye.

End of transcript.
